findings.title: Same NPE race remains in the getSubGroupsStream overloads
findings.body: The fix only guards `getSubGroupsCount()` against `modelSupplier.get()` returning `null` (group concurrently removed from the DB while a cached entry is still served). The three `getSubGroupsStream(...)` overloads (lines 256, 262 and 268) dereference `modelSupplier.get()` unconditionally, so the very same race that produced the reported NPE still throws `NullPointerException` there, e.g. when the admin endpoint lists sub-groups with paging/search while another request deletes the group. Either handle `null` consistently (empty stream / delegate invalidation) or centralize the null handling in one helper so all accessors are protected.

findings.title: getSubGroupsCount() can now return null, an undocumented value for GroupModel
findings.body: `GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount()` is declared to return `Long` but no provider (JPA, map) ever returns `null`; callers therefore assume a non-null count. After this change the cached adapter returns `null` when the group has vanished from the store, which only moves the failure: any caller that unboxes the value (`long c = group.getSubGroupsCount()`, arithmetic or comparison) will throw NPE at a less obvious place, and `GroupRepresentation.subGroupCount` will be serialized as null/absent for that group, which the admin console does not expect. Prefer returning `0L` (or invalidating/handling the missing group explicitly) instead of leaking `null` through the model API.

findings.title: Regression test is racy: reader thread is never joined before asserting
findings.body: `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti` starts a reader thread and then immediately asserts `caughtExceptions` is empty after `deletedAll.set(true)`, without joining the thread. The thread may not even have issued its first request before the deletions finish, and an exception thrown by an in-flight request can be added to the list after the assertion has run. The test can therefore pass even when the NPE it is supposed to cover is still present (false negative), and it can also fail spuriously. Join the thread (or use an ExecutorService/Future and get its result) before asserting.

findings.title: Non-daemon reader thread can leak/hang the test JVM
findings.body: The reader thread spins on `while (!deletedAll.get())` and `deletedAll` is only set after the delete loop completes. If any `groups().group(groupUuid).remove()` call throws (404, 500, connection error) the flag is never set, and since the thread is a plain non-daemon `Thread` with no timeout it keeps looping forever, hammering the server and preventing JVM/test-run termination. Set `deletedAll` in a `finally` block, mark the thread as daemon, and/or bound the loop with a deadline.

findings.title: Reader thread busy-loops admin REST calls with no pause
findings.body: The reader thread repeatedly calls `groups().groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true)` in a tight loop with no sleep for the whole duration of 100 group deletions. This issues an unbounded number of full group listings (each with maxResults=Integer.MAX_VALUE), consuming CPU on both test and server side and slowing CI considerably. A small sleep between iterations, or a bounded iteration count, would reproduce the race just as well.

findings.title: New test does not drain the 200 admin events it generates
findings.body: The realm used by this class has `eventsEnabled(true)` and other tests in the class assert on specific entries from `adminEvents.poll()` / call `adminEvents.skipAll()`. `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti` creates and deletes 100 groups (200 admin events) without polling or skipping them; if the injected admin-events queue is shared across tests in the class this leaves stale events that will make the subsequent `adminEvents.poll()` assertions fail or match the wrong event. Add `adminEvents.skipAll()` at the end of the test (or clear the queue) to be safe.
